title: Ambipolar metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe2
authors: Ha-Leem Kim, Hyungbin Lim, Terry Wu, Amogh Y. Waghmare, Garima Gupta, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Archana Raja, Eric Y. Ma, Feng Wang
abstract: When Coulomb interactions dominate kinetic energy, dilute two-dimensional carriers form a Wigner solid. Both its melting and disorder-driven localization can drive density-tuned metal-insulator transitions, but their relative roles and interplay have been debated for decades. Atomically thin semiconductors offer a new test because transport and scanning tunneling microscopy can probe the same material, yet poor contacts impede transport where correlations are strongest. Here we introduce contact-free radio-frequency reflectometry that senses sheet resistance through capacitive gate coupling. It resolves the electron and previously inaccessible hole transitions in the same bilayer MoSe2 device, whose carriers share disorder but not mass. Their critical densities differ fourfold yet correspond to comparable Coulomb-to-kinetic-energy ratios, where tunneling microscopy finds solid-liquid coexistence. Magnetoresistance peaks sharply at each transition, reflecting a Pomeranchuk-like, field-driven expansion of the Wigner solid against the correlated liquid. Our results demonstrate interaction-driven transitions in high-quality two-dimensional semiconductors, opening quantitative transport in contact-limited systems.
summary: This work reports on the ambipolar metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe2 using advanced contact-free radio-frequency reflectometry. By measuring both electron and hole transport, the authors provide strong evidence that the MIT is governed by strong electron-electron interactions, leading to Wigner crystallization. This opens a quantitative transport window for studying correlated states in high-quality 2D semiconductors.
main_problem: The paper investigates the metal-insulator transition (MIT) in two dimensions, specifically resolving the long-standing debate over whether Coulomb interactions or disorder primarily drive this transition.
main_result: The study demonstrates interaction-driven MITs in bilayer MoSe2 for both electrons and holes, evidenced by comparable Wigner-Seitz radii at transition, and maps the transition using contact-free RF reflectometry.
method: The authors employed contact-free radio-frequency (RF) reflectometry to measure sheet resistance and magnetotransport properties in the bilayer semiconductor.
model_or_system: The physical system is bilayer MoSe2, a semiconductor used to study ambipolar transport. The measurements probe the transition between a correlated liquid and a Wigner solid state.
key_observables: Sheet resistance (R) vs. carrier density, Magnetoresistance (MR) peaks, and resonance frequency ($f_0$) shifts.
important_parameters: Wigner-Seitz radii ($r_s$), critical densities ($n_c$), and the ratio of Coulomb interaction energy to kinetic energy.
main_assumptions: The RF readout is non-perturbative, and the analysis compares results to theoretical benchmarks derived from disorder-free, symmetric gate geometries.
figures_summary: Figures show RF spectra, extracted sheet resistance vs. density (for both electron and hole doping), and magnetotransport ratios mapping the MIT.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents the experimental setup, characterizes the ambipolar MIT using RF measurements, analyzes the temperature and magnetic field dependence of the transition, and compares findings to theoretical models of correlated electron systems.
why_interesting: The work provides quantitative transport measurements in a clean, tunable 2D system, offering experimental validation for theoretical models describing strongly correlated phases like Wigner crystals.
